title: EDGE: DCGain wrong finite value / wrong Inf next to near-DC or exact DC poles
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). DCGain disagrees with FreqResponse(0) and the exact rational oracle when the DC solve is near-singular: absolute coefficient floors drop tiny B, transfer-limit path returns neither Inf nor the exact value, MIMO near-DC poles, and an exactly singular dense block missed by dcGainByBlockLaurent. All pre-existing on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #16 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value at a reachable, observable continuous integrator (MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: sys := &System{A: [[0,0],[1,-1.3258457598967608e-08]], B: [7.29653485561532e-14; 1.0337733234010072e-13], C: [0 1], D: [0]} (continuous). DCGain gives 7.797085843999098e-06/nil; FreqResponse(0) gives +Inf. G(s) = (1.03e-13 s + 7.30e-14)/(s(s+1.33e-8)), so G(0) = Inf. The value equals B2/1.3258e-8, i.e. B1 was dropped as zero. The likely cause is the absolute coefficient floor in dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit or dcGainByStructuralEntries for tiny B (response.go). The branch gives the same result as base 2e4a07d. The sweep found 13 more TF.StateSpace realizations with a trailing-zero den (exact pole at s=0) where DCGain returns 0 and FR(0) returns +Inf.

[w12 #17 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value with the wrong sign and magnitude when the transfer limit is reached with a computed pole near DC. Repro (continuous companion): A row0 = -[6.325495602920146 12.427798551146598 7.785922515524618 2.9590313755032033e-05 2.830045401741772e-11 5.223977207934464e-19], subdiagonal ones, B=e1, C=[-0.1661821972150368 0.6204228877798674 1.5965704467083484 -0.2679049847206111 -0.17326373644234616 -0.9184631132625503], D=0.18013697908513038. The exact big.Rat G(0) is -1.758e18, FreqResponse(0) is +Inf, and ddResponseInto gives the exact value. Correct answers would be Inf (pole at DC) or -1.76e18; 9.7e11 is neither. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Same result on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #18 freq/review2] Pre-existing (identical on base and branch), DCGain wrong next to near-DC poles in MIMO state-space models: for 49 of 1400 sweep models DCGain is +/-Inf or off while FreqResponse(0) matches the exact oracle. Files: response.go (DCGain explicit solve / dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go. Oracle: exact rational solve of C(s0 I-A)^-1 B+D.

[w12 #41 dcgain/review1] DCGain finite for an exactly singular dense block with no 1x1 exact pole (pre-existing, same on base 2e4a07d and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,2,2, A=[0.38629023905802873 3.851534645926291 -3.23782488498432; 0 4 -3; 4 1.6251019182011088 -4.625101918201109], B=[-0.5 0; -1.75 0; 0 0], C=[-1 -2.176206339653932 1; 0 -0.06848213510526557 0], D=[5.737696031494993 0; 0.75 0], dt=0.1). title: EDGE: Care state scale() ignores R; cheap-control default mode fails, retry costs 2x
body:
Found in wave 18 (fix/wave18).

[w18 #4 riccati/INY4MG] State scaling makes cheap-control Care much worse than no scaling. Repro: the sweep above (PCG seed 7,11; n=5, m=2; A=0.4*N(0,1); B=N(0,1); Q=MM'*10^U(3,6); R=LL'*10^U(-15,-11)). Before d435244 there were 914 default-only Care failures out of 3000 against 32 NoScaling-only; the INY4MG case 'modeOnly' in riccati_care_verify_test.go is one of them. Files: matrix_equation_problem.go scale(), riccati.go hamiltonianSolution, pencilSolution, lastResort. Evidence: scale() balances A, B and Q/S but ignores R, so under R much smaller than B'XB every cost scale fails (modeOnly trace: state-scaled sigma=1 found 4 stable eigenvalues, sigma=2.98e-8 found 6, sigma=3.05e-5 gave an unstable A-BK; unscaled sigma=1 residual 4e-3, which Newton refines to 6e-11). The retry in d435244 covers this at twice the cost on those inputs; making scale() account for R would remove the cause.

title: EDGE: TunePID ideal-screen fail-closed path for descriptor/non-SISO plants untested (HVXYLI rest)
body:
Found in wave 18 (fix/wave18). HVXYLI merged partial in w18; remainder: cover the final-transfer-path unresolved() branch with a test and confirm full-suite/amd64 validation of 78fca45.

[w18 #19 pidtune/HVXYLI] Owner awareness: descriptor (E!=nil) or non-SISO plants with an ideal derivative that reach the final transfer path now fail closed on an undecided float verdict. Base returned the float value. No test covers this path.

[w18 #25 pidtune/HVXYLI PARTIAL] HVXYLI is fixed in commit 78fca45 on fix/pidtune-wave18 in pid_tuning.go, but the full test suite and the amd64 run did not finish, so validation is incomplete and the status is partial.

The bug, reproduced first: a plant of order 16 or less with n+lag above 64 kept an undecided float verdict. A hidden mode at 1−9.99e-11 is a root outside |z|<1−1e-10, and at lag 70 base returned stable; exact Schur–Cohn says unstable. A mode at 1−3e-10 also passed as stable at lag 70 without being certified. The new test fails on base and passes now.

What changed in pidTuningIdealStable: every loop outside exact scope now follows one chain: float verdict, then exact Schur–Cohn when n+lag ≤ 64, then the closed-loop realization's float and Bauer–Fike verdicts, then fail closed as unstable. This removes the #34 exception in two places: the n+lag>64 early return, and the final transfer-path `return stable` (now `return unresolved()`).

Bauer–Fike radius: it now adds the eigen-solve residual. R = AV − VΛ is computed, and eta grows by ‖R‖_F·√(Σ1/s_i²) for the unit-column eigenvectors V. In practice this term is tiny, so no test pins it.

pidTuningIdealExact now checks n+lag > 64 before building the characteristic. That cut the n18lag60 screen bench from 5128 to 120 allocs/op and B/op by 28%.

Fail-closed band (2nd-order core, hidden mode 1−e, lag 70): e ≥ 3e-5 is decided by the characteristic float verdict, e = 1e-5 is rescued by the realization/Bauer–Fike step, and e ≤ 1e-6 now fails closed. Base passed those last ones as stable on an undecided verdict.

No value→error regressions found: TunePID and Pidtune results were identical between base 8de590a and the candidate over 315 cases. These were 7 discrete plants (first/second/third-order, integrating, oscillatory, unstable; dt 0.1/0.5) with delays of 3–10 s (lag 6–100), families PID, PD and PI, at default and two fixed wc.

Behaviour change outside the repro: models that can't be realized (descriptor E≠nil, or not SISO) that reach the final transfer path now fail closed on an undecided float verdict, where base kept the float value. This follows the decision's "one chain everywhere".

Not done: the AMWRJU MathWorks 'PD' check. It was listed as a track decision, not part of HVXYLI.

Precision limits: none found.

title: EDGE: descriptor norms: pow2 equilibration before kappa(E) test; singular E keeps error (decided)
body:
Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). [w15 #28 norms/JA65GD] JA65GD step 2, singular E in H2Norm/HinfNorm/Norm (owner decision needed). The MathWorks norm (control/ref/dynamicsystem.norm.html) and hinfnorm (robust/ref/dynamicsystem.hinfnorm.html) pages say nothing about dss, improper or singular-E models, so the precondition for implementing it is not met. Repro: NewDescriptor(A=[-1 1;0.5 -2], B=[1;1], C=[1 0], D=0, E=diag(1,0)) gives H2Norm/HinfNorm -> ErrDescriptorUnsupported wrapping ErrDescriptorSingular. When decided: properExplicitForm / conversionStandardForm (descriptor.go) already reduce proper index-1 models exactly. A continuous improper model plausibly gives Inf for both norms. A discrete improper (non-causal) model has bounded gain on the unit circle, so 'improper means Inf' does not follow there; the owner must settle that case.

[w15 #29 norms/JA65GD] Owner review of the cond(E) limit for norms: normDescriptorCondLimit = 1/sqrt(eps) ≈ 6.7e7 (descriptor.go). A legitimately stiff diagonal E, e.g. diag(1, 1e-9), still returns ErrDescriptorUnsupported. Base also errored, so no regression; loosen it if the owner prefers.

[w15 #30 norms/review0] JA65GD step 2 (planned, not a bug): support singular or improper descriptor E in H2Norm/HinfNorm/Norm after checking the MathWorks hinfnorm/norm docs. Also consider equilibrating E before the kappa guard, so that badly scaled diagonal E like diag(1e-8,1) is accepted (descriptor.go normExplicitForm).

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-21; MathWorks norm/hinfnorm pages checked)
- Equilibration is not a policy question: do pow2 row/column scaling (E→LER, A→LAR, B→LB, C→CR) before the κ(E) test. It is an exact equivalence, so the transfer function is unchanged. Keep the κ(E) error afterwards.
- Singular/improper E: neither page says anything about improper or singular-E models; they only say H∞ = Inf for unstable systems and H2 = Inf when unstable or continuous with nonzero D. Parity is undefined, so keep the documented error for singular E.
- LOW priority: this is feature scope behind the correctness backlog.

title: EDGE: AbsorbIO: keep non-decomposable residual as shared internal delays (minimality improvement; AY2CYR closed)
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). AY2CYR partial merged (58fbbe4 tie-break). Remaining duplication argued structural; MATLAB has no IO-only absorb target.

[w17 #69 edges] AY2CYR: decide between (a) closing as partial / won't-fix, since one copy of the internal delays per piece is structural and MATLAB has no IO-only absorb to match, and (b) a new task to keep the non-decomposable residual as shared internal delays with the decomposable input and output delays absorbed as states. For the test plant (b) gives n=4, q=4, against today's n=7, q=4. Both are AbsorbIO in delay_residual_split.go.

[w17 #73 edges] AY2CYR reproduced. With n=1, m=3, p=2, a non-decomposable SetDelay, OutputDelay set, and 2 internal LFT delays: continuous AbsorbDelay(AbsorbIO) gives q=4 (2 column pieces) and discrete gives q=6 (3 column pieces). The response still matches the original. In the general case this cannot be soundly fixed:
(1) The duplication is structural, not a copying bug. Each split piece is out_g * G * in_g. A diagonal output delay does not commute with a non-diagonal G, so every group needs its own copy of the states, and the internal-delay loop (B2/C2/D22, Tau) goes with each copy. Sharing Tau channels across pieces would give a wrong model.
(2) For discrete AbsorbIO, the existing per-group cost (n + sum of in/out delay samples) is exactly the realized state count, so the base already picks the split with the fewest states. Weighting internal delays in the cost only trades states for channels. I tried it: discrete repro went 27 states/6 channels -> 33/4, with neither dominating, so I reverted it.
(3) MATLAB parity sets no achievable target. MATLAB ss has no IODelay matrix: a non-decomposable IODelay already becomes InternalDelay at construction, so "MATLAB keeps the original internal delays" describes a different model. It is not something this absorption path can match.
Delivered the one strictly better change (commit 58fbbe4, branch fix/edges-wave17, delay_residual_split.go newResidualDelaySplit). When row and column costs tie and the model has internal delays, pick the split with fewer pieces. Same state count, fewer duplicated internal-delay channels. q=0 behaviour is unchanged. Example: Delay [[3,1,0],[1,0,0]], dt=1, n=1, internal Tau [3,2]. AbsorbIO goes from 7 states/6 internal delays to 7/4. PullDelaysToLFT goes from 3 states/9 delays to 2/7. The original repro (no tie) is unchanged. A model with redundant internal delays is still correct; it is just not minimal.

[w17 #74 edges] QFAIOB is fixed (commit 91bca71 on fix/edges-wave17). AY2CYR reproduces but I left it alone: it needs a coordinator decision.

QFAIOB: I reproduced the bug. With A at scale 1e298 or 1e-300, 5 of the 6 points just off a real pole (all but λ≈-6.7e297) gave EvalFr = NaN with a nil error, while ddResponseInto had the right finite value. The fix is in /Users/josephj/workspace/controlsys/.claude/worktrees/wf_b27620d1-19f-28/frequency_hessenberg.go. A new helper, finiteResponse(dst), now runs at the end of both balancedDense.evalInto and hessenbergSweep.evalInto. If any output entry is NaN or Inf it returns errSingularPencil, which is not errNonFinitePencil, so evalWithPoleLimitGated goes on to the ddResponseInto / pole-limit fallback. All 6 repro points now match ddResponseInto. That includes the reviewer's case (b) at sc=1e-300, where base gave a wrong -2.0.

New test: TestEvalFrExtremeScaleNearPole in frequency_graded_test.go. The oracle is exact scale invariance: scaling A and B by a power of two (2^990 and 2^-996), and s by the same factor, leaves the response unchanged, so the unit-scale model gives the reference value. It checks EvalFr and both solvers through evalWithPoleLimit at s=λ(1-1e-10) for each real eigenvalue, with relative tolerance 1e-5. With the source change removed the test fails with NaN on 15 checks.

Benchmarks (benchcmp, base 7c14e32 against the working tree): +2.4% geomean, worst +5.8% (FreqResponseWithDelay), no extra allocations. Nothing near a 2x slowdown.

AY2CYR (not fixed, coordinator decision needed): it reproduces as described, q=4 against the reviewer's target of 2. I think the duplication is structural. The response is y = Σ_g Dout_g·H12·K·H21·Din_g·u_g, where K = Δ(I−H22Δ)⁻¹ is the internal-delay loop. The output delays Dout_g differ from piece to piece, and a single shared K loses which piece its output belongs to. So any realization that turns IO delays into states needs one copy of K per piece. The "MATLAB 2" target is also not something MATLAB does: MATLAB stores a non-decomposable ioDelay on an ss model as internal delays, and its absorbDelay on a discrete model absorbs every delay, internal ones included. There is no IO-only absorb mode to match.

For this test plant (total delay [[4,2,1],[1,0,0]], dt=1), the reviewer's alternative works out like this. The best split is input delay [1,0,0] plus output delay [1,0], leaving 2 residual entries ([2,1,0] on output 1). Absorbing the input and output delays as shifts and keepin


## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-22)
Close AY2CYR as done. The duplication is non-minimality by construction: the delay loop must travel with each non-commuting piece, the response matches, and MATLAB has no IO-only absorb. Option (b), shared internal delays, is filed as an EDGE improvement.

title: EDGE: Stabsep/Modsep fail closed on index>=2 descriptors and rejected Dgges reorders
body:
Found in wave 18 (fix/wave18). Remainder of 4U3MDS (merged w18). Needs infinite-structure deflation before QZ.

[w18 #9 riccati/4U3MDS] Index 2 or higher descriptors now fail closed in Stabsep/Modsep (MATLAB parity gap, not a wrong value). QZ only resolves a length-k infinite Jordan chain to |β|/|α| ~ ε^(1/k), and certifyFiniteRetained now rejects these instead of splitting them. Distinct, well-resolved poles inside the eps^(1/m) cluster window are reported as a K=0 multiple-pole breakaway, and a complex stationary point is returned as a real breakaway, listed twice once per conjugate root. The window is clusterRadius(m, scale) = min((1e3*n*eps)^(1/m), 1e-4) * max(|Re r|, min(||A||_1, 1)). For m=3 and n=3 that is about 8.7e-5*scale, and the scale is 1 for any realization with ||A|| >= 1. The same rho also bounds |Im r|. So at unit scale, three poles within about 1e-4 are merged. Any pole set slower than about 1e-4 in a unit-norm realization (a companion form or any rotation) is merged as a whole. title: PERF: EvalFr balancedDense/hessenbergSweep normwise pivot tol sends graded models to dd fallback
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). Correct values, slow path (O(n^3) double-double per point). Componentwise pivot test on failure branch.

[w17 #68 edges] PERF (not wrong values): balancedDense.evalInto and hessenbergSweep.factor still use the normwise pivot tolerance n*scale*eps. Graded but finite realizations (e.g. a companion form of a wide-range polynomial TF) are therefore flagged singular at every point. They now get the correct value via the double-double fallback, which is O(n^3) double-double per point plus a pole search (poleSpacing). A componentwise pivot test on the failure branch only (track the row magnitudes the pivot was formed from; singular iff pivot <= n*eps*mag), with Hessenberg failures retried on a lazily built balancedDense, would keep such sweeps on the fast path. Files: frequency_hessenberg.go.

title: Pidtune ~6-8x slower on simple auto calls since AUOTFB first-design gate (owner decision on gate grid)
body:
Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

Perf (CR7GLM, caused by AUOTFB): newPidtuneGate now runs on every automatic Pidtune call. It evaluates the plant about 3000 times (sens grid about 230 points/decade, cross grid 100/decade, no shared points, band floor*1e-3 to wc*1e3). Result: about 8x slower on BenchmarkPidtune_PI/PID/PIDF (93us to 760us, 25KB to 388KB/op) and +66% on the continuous-delay sweep. Options: share or interpolate the sens and cross plant samples, cheaper pole-residue evaluation of the SISO plant on the grids, or lazy top-down |S| scanning. Files: pidtune.go (newPidtuneGate, pidtuneGate.sensitivityOver, crossExcess). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune.

Pidtune slowdown on simple plants from 027664e (AUOTFB first-design gate). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune. Evidence, 8cfed86 to HEAD: Pidtune_PI 80 us to 711 us (+787%), PID +836%, PIDF +751%, PidtuneFastSampled/O2 42 us to 797 us (+1795%), O5 +429%, Delayed/PI +185%, Delayed/PD 1.0 ms to 15 ms (+1358%), Delayed/PIDF +142%; B/op 25 KB to 388 KB, allocs/op +42% to +60% (Delayed/PD +2190%, of which my commits recover 8.6%). The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP is +7% (3.52 to 3.77 ms) after the crossover scan moved to the finer |S| grid (16add00). Repro: benchcmp -base b0e01b5 -candidate 9b2e8d4 -bench ^BenchmarkPidtune. Most of it is bisection and golden-section refinement calls into the memoized p.at during back-off steps that fail anyway.

body:

[w13 #56 fuzz/MOI6LA] [EDGE] FRDFeedback with more plant inputs than outputs solves the m x m system I - sign*K*G with an absolute pivot tolerance (cSolveInPlace). The exact answer is G/(1+GK), about 4.63-1.71i. Files: frd.go FRDFeedback, frequency.go cSolveInPlace. Fix: solve the smaller p x p I - sign*G*K when p < m, or use a relative pivot test.
